chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Song lyrics on playing cards clipped to the guitar
summary: Lu describes Danny's practice of pasting lyrics on cards and clipping them to his guitar neck so he could sing every song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: He would write songs and then got a deck of cards, and he would take this deck...you know, the words of the songs, and paste it on these cards and put it on his guitar -- and he would sing from that, you know. So one night I told my girlfriend, Rosie, and I said, "We're going

to Hoboken where Danny works." So she said, "Yes." So when we got there, I said, "Now, Rose, now Danny's going to sing all night." So she says, "All right, I ain't gonna laugh." So finally, Danny started singing, "Baby, Won't You Please Come Home." And Rose started laughing. She said, "Do you know all the words to that?" I said, "Rose, don't do that." And Danny kept on singing, and kept on singing. And that's how he would learn... She said, "What is that...?" I said, "That's the words he's got on the neck of his guitar." He would put the words on the back of the card...
Keep that, because I want you to play a little something for me, Danny.

All right. And you'd stick it right... Yuo see, I had a clothespin that I put here, and I'd hook this thing right in the clothespin. So I'm playing and I look at the words. The people don't know what you're doing, and the people don't care, because they're half-drunk, you know...
As long as you're singing, that's all they can hear.
It's a survival thing with me. I don't care who laughs and who didn't laugh.
